resources.string: Keep an authenticated ADB TCP listener for restarts without Wi-Fi during this boot. The listener may be reachable from connected networks. Applies on the next start. Turning this off stops future activation. An existing listener remains until ADB restarts.

Monitor the backend and retry when it stops, with an ongoing notification. Start manually once to resume after Stop. Boot recovery also requires Start on boot. Pairing, a usable ADB endpoint and manufacturer background settings still apply.
Reuse local ADB TCP first, then wireless debugging. Enable TCP on start while Wi-Fi is available before trying offline restarts. A reboot may require Wi-Fi again.
No recovery attempt yet. Tap to refresh.
Try a temporary local-only hotspot and wireless debugging when no Wi-Fi network is connected. Requires ADB pairing, WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS and a hotspot permission. Device support varies.

This requests a temporary local-only hotspot and repeatedly asks Android to enable wireless debugging for up to 120 seconds. It can affect Wi-Fi and hotspot operation. Android or the manufacturer may refuse the attempt.

Allow Nearby devices on Android 13 or later, or precise Location on Android 11–12. Location services may also be needed on those older versions.

Enable TCP on start for later offline restarts. Boot recovery requires Start on boot and the first device unlock. Automatic offline attempts are limited to three, with at least five minutes between failed attempts. A manual start retries immediately.
Grant WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS through ADB first, then enable this option.\n\nadb shell pm grant %1$s android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS
Hotspot permission was denied. Allow Nearby devices (Android 13+) or precise Location (Android 11–12) in app permissions, then enable this option again.
